suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-35 adds this relationship only as a bounded Brugada ventricular-arrhythmia risk association. A Québec cohort examined predictors of ventricular arrhythmias and sudden death in Brugada syndrome, but risk-stratification evidence does not establish that every cardiac-arrhythmia diagnosis in a person with Brugada syndrome was caused by the syndrome. Require independently diagnosed Brugada syndrome with documented type-1 ECG phenotype or specialist electrophysiology confirmation, and separately documented ventricular arrhythmia or qualifying arrhythmic event with compatible chronology. Do not infer arrhythmia from a Brugada pattern alone, palpitations, syncope without evaluation, or family history. Preserve structural heart disease, ischemia, channelopathy overlap, electrolyte disturbance, fever or drug triggers, and other arrhythmia causes.
evidenceGaps: Independent electrophysiology documentation of Brugada syndrome and type-1 ECG phenotype or equivalent specialist confirmation
Separately documented ventricular arrhythmia or qualifying arrhythmic event with ECG, monitoring, or device records
Chronology, fever or medication triggers, electrophysiology findings, and treatment context
Assessment of structural heart disease, ischemia, electrolyte disturbance, channelopathy overlap, and other causes
Cardiology or electrophysiology assessment of the individual's phenotype and competing explanations

sourceReferences.citation: Rivard L, Roux A, Nault I, Champagne J, Roux JF, Tadros R, et al. Predictors of Ventricular Arrhythmias and Sudden Death in a Québec Cohort With Brugada Syndrome. Canadian Journal of Cardiology. 2016;32(11):1355.e1-1355.e7. PMID 27378596. doi:10.1016/j.cjca.2016.03.012.
sourceReferences.note: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-35 Brugada cohort evidence for the bounded ventricular-arrhythmia proposition. Mapping approval is not citation verification; this source remains pending qualified-human review.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 27378596; Québec cohort evaluating ventricular arrhythmia and sudden-death predictors in Brugada syndrome; approved ME-35 guard requires ventricular phenotype and competing-cause review.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The Brugada cohort supports risk stratification for ventricular arrhythmia and sudden death, without establishing an individual cardiac-arrhythmia nexus.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR section 3.310 is established; ECG phenotype, arrhythmic event, chronology, trigger context, and competing cardiac causes require individual review.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Brugada-related cardiac sodium-channel dysfunction may create an electrical substrate vulnerable to ventricular arrhythmia, with fever, drugs, autonomic state, and other modifiers affecting risk, but the individual's arrhythmic pathway remains hypothesized until electrophysiologic records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. The cohort identifies ventricular-arrhythmia risk factors in Brugada syndrome but does not prove that any particular arrhythmia was caused by the syndrome.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Brugada ECG/electrophysiology confirmation; objective ventricular-arrhythmia records; chronology and fever/drug triggers; treatment context; and evaluation of structural, ischemic, electrolyte, overlapping-channelopathy, and other causes.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Fever or medication-triggered arrhythmia without established Brugada attribution
Other inherited channelopathy or arrhythmia substrate
